items.accessibility:
- The field is a real new-password input labelled Password; the eye is a toggle button with aria-pressed. Each rule is a list item that says done or not yet, and every check placed or taken back is announced from a status region.
- Hide is decoration (aria-hidden). He is an illustration shipped inside hide-art.ts as two WebP data URIs (43KB of images, 59KB as text), so the install is complete with nothing to put in public/; his pupil, tongue, blush, colour change and hop are drawn in code over it.
- One frame loop outside React writes his styles and sleeps when he’s still; his breathing is a compositor animation. The tongue is drawn in an overlay over the block and costs no React renders.
- The stage is the lit --primary surface engraved with fine scales; he blends into whatever colour your theme gives it, light or dark. Tongue, pupil, blush and check colours are --hide-* variables you can override. No drop shadows, glow or blur.
- With reduced motion there is no tongue, hop or breathing: checks appear in place and his colour changes in place.
- Built from Password input, Status button and Text morph, which the CLI installs with it. No animation library.

states.title: spotted
states.description: Hide sits on his branch in full colour, his pupil following the caret (or the pointer between keystrokes); the line above reads “Hide is easy to spot”. He breathes and blinks now and then.

states.title: catch
states.description: A rule met: he glances at its circle and his tongue shoots out (150ms), touches it, and the check pops in and draws itself as the tongue comes back (210ms). Several at once go one after another, faster.

states.title: exposed

states.title: startle

states.title: breached

states.title: saved

states.title: napping
states.description: Coo stands on his post at the left of the lit stage, the red mailbox with its flag up at the right and his dashed route between them. While the resend clock runs he dozes: his eye shuts, a z drifts up from his cap every 1.1s, and a thought bubble rolls the seconds down; the line reads “Coo is catching his breath”.

states.title: typing
states.description: Typing wakes him for 4s (“Coo is reading along”): each digit rises into its box and he nods forward from his feet.

states.title: checking

states.title: wrong
states.description: onVerify returns false or throws: Coo shakes his head, the boxes shake, turn red and clear from the right; the line reads “Not the code Coo carried”.

states.title: right
states.description: The boxes close into one pill with a drawn check, Coo puffs his chest with two flaps and a hop, and the resend line folds away; “Signed for. You’re in.”

states.title: ready
states.description: At zero the bubble shrinks away into a blur, he wakes with a hop, the line reads “Coo is ready to fly again” and “Resend in 0:00” turns into Resend code.

states.title: resend
states.description: Coo takes off with an envelope (1s along the route, with real wingbeats), waits over the mailbox until onResend settles, pops the flag and flies home empty; Sent, then the clock starts again.

states.title: send failed
states.description: onResend throws: he turns back with the envelope still in his beak, the line says “Coo couldn’t get through” and Resend shakes into Try again.

- Releasing early, leaving the button, losing focus, Escape or a hidden browser tab cancels an incomplete hold. A completed action continues through its promise.
- State announcements live outside the button. The button retains focus while pending or showing its result.
- Reduced motion removes icon movement and spinning. The functional progress ring still communicates the hold duration.
- Use clear action labels and provide undo in your application where appropriate.

items.accessibility:
- A native button provides keyboard browsing. Paste files while focus is inside the component. File results are announced through live regions, and each progress bar is labelled with its file name.
- Drag listeners belong to the drop area, so multiple uploaders can sit on a page independently. No window listeners, proximity targets or perpetual animation loop.
- Remove, replacement and unmount abort the relevant uploads. Late progress or promise results from a cancelled attempt are ignored. Retry starts a fresh attempt.
- Duplicates are compared by file name, size, MIME type and last-modified time. Remove a file to select it again.
- All supporting files ship together, along with Text morph and Number roll for the original quiet label and progress feedback. No animation library or additional stylesheet keyframes.
- Reduced motion keeps labels, numbers and status icons in place. Feedback remains visible as text, a check and progress.

items.accessibility: Native button supports Enter and Space to browse, and focused paste. File updates are announced politely; progress bars are labelled; retry and remove actions name their file. Files appear directly as attachment cards. Reduced motion disables membrane bending, card entry motion and shimmer. Attachment icons and labels animate within a persistent card, and reduced motion uses immediate state changes. Upload and retry actions transfer focus to the stable remove button.

items.accessibility:
- Each wheel is a spinbutton with aria-valuetext (the option and its unit). Arrow keys step, Page Up and Down jump five, Home and End go to the ends.
- A tap on a row above or below the lens turns it to the middle; the row is found from the drum's angle, not the flat offset, so rows near the rim land correctly.
- Every wheel has 18 faces whatever its length: only faces turning round the back are relabelled, so 60 minutes or 100 years cost the same. Turning writes two transforms a frame and renders nothing through React.
- The drum leaves a hole under the lens through its mask, so the lens copy is the only text there; mouse wheels over the picker turn it instead of scrolling the page.
- Reduced motion turns the wheel straight to the row instead of decaying onto it; dragging still follows the pointer.

items.accessibility:
- The input is a combobox with a listbox of suggestions: arrows move the highlight, Enter picks it (the first match is ready while you type), Escape closes the list and Down opens it again.
- Chips are a list. Left arrow or Backspace at the start of the input moves to the last chip; arrows, Home and End move between chips; Backspace or Enter edits one, Delete removes it, Escape returns to the input. Each remove button is named after its chip.
- Adds, duplicates, invalid values, removals and resolved names are announced in a status region outside the field. The error under the field is linked to the input with aria-describedby.
- Every change notes where the chips sit at the keystroke, lets React lay out the new order, then glides each chip from its old place with an additive transform, so a name that resolves while a paste is still landing adds its own glide instead of restarting anything. Leaving and flying copies live in an overlay so the list never waits for them. Nothing runs between changes.
- On touch screens the input uses 16px text so phones don't zoom into it; the chip's letters scale down to 13px as the shell grows.
- Reduced motion adds, removes and resolves in place; colour, icons and the line under the field still say what happened.

items.accessibility:
- The avatar is a button: Enter or Space opens the file picker, and paste takes a photo from the clipboard while focus is anywhere in the field. Dropping a file on the avatar or the stage opens it.
- The stage is focusable: arrow keys move the photo (Shift for bigger steps), plus and minus zoom, R rotates, Enter saves and Escape cancels. The zoom slider is a native range input; the zoom is announced when it settles, never while it moves.
- One frame loop with fixed 4ms steps writes transforms to three nested layers (move, zoom, turn) and sleeps once everything is still; React only hears about it then. The layers are promoted while they move and released after, so the photo is redrawn sharp at its new size.
- Only the stage takes touch (touch-action: none); the page itself is never locked. Wheel and trackpad pinch zoom about the pointer and don't scroll the page while over the photo.
- The crop is drawn from the original at full resolution with the same transform you see, so what lands in the circle is what you saved.
- Reduced motion opens and closes in place and the photo goes straight to its bounds instead of springing.

items.accessibility:
- The hours are a focusable group: arrow keys move a slot outline, Enter adds an event there, Page Up and Page Down change the range. Tab reaches the events.
- On an event, arrow keys move it by a step or a day, Shift with up or down changes its length, Enter renames it and Delete removes it. Each change is announced with the new day and times, and any clash.
- Each event is labelled with its title, day and times; busy time is a note, so it's read but never focused.
- Gestures report a change of step, not every pointer move, so a drag re-renders a handful of times a second; events move with eased top, left, width and height on their own layer while held.
- On touch the hours scroll as usual; holding 360ms picks up (with a short vibration where supported), and only then does the page stop scrolling under the finger.
- Reduced motion moves events in place, without glides, slides or shakes; rings, colours and announcements still say what happened.

items.accessibility:
- The field is a real textarea labelled by label, so screen readers, spellcheck, undo and the clipboard behave as anywhere else. Errors and the character count are linked with aria-describedby and marked aria-invalid; saves and refusals are announced in a status region outside the field.
- Text and field use the same letters in the same box with kerning and ligatures off, so focusing never moves a glyph. Line breaks pasted into a title become spaces.
- A refusal that arrives while you are already typing something newer keeps your new text and only shows the reason. Results from an older save are ignored.
- Type is inherited: set font size, weight and tracking on the component or its parent. On touch screens, text under 16px makes iOS zoom in when it is focused; set a 16px minimum on phones if that matters for your layout.
- Reduced motion changes everything in place: no morphs, shakes or easing; the colours and words still say what happened.

states.title: rest
states.description: Plain text in your own type. Under a mouse, a 1px frame sized by the text fades in over 160ms; it extends 0.4em either side, with negative margins, so the text stays aligned with what is around it.

states.title: edit
states.description: A click focuses the field at the point you clicked (double-click selects a word); Tab, Enter or F2 select everything. The frame turns to the focus colour in 200ms. The field grows with the text: one-line fields widen, wrapped titles take more lines.

states.title: save
states.description: Enter or leaving the field calls onSave with the trimmed value. The new text stays where it is; a 14px slot opens beside one-line text (380ms) with a spinner, then a check draws itself (420ms) and the slot closes 1.4s later. Wrapped titles say Saving, then Saved, in the line below.

states.title: stored
states.description: If onSave returns a different string, the text morphs into it: shared letters glide, new ones rise out of a blur, and one-line text eases to its new width.

states.title: refused
states.description: If validate returns a message or onSave throws, the field opens again with what you typed, shakes ±4px over 380ms, its frame turns red and the reason folds open under it. Typing clears the red.

states.title: cancel
states.description: Escape morphs the text back to the saved value and keeps focus on the field; Enter edits it again. An emptied name cancels the same way unless allowEmpty is set.

states.title: elsewhere
states.description: A new value prop while you are not editing morphs in (wrapped titles crossfade whole and ease to their new height in 420ms). While you are editing, your text is left alone and Escape goes back to the newer name.

states.title: limit

items.accessibility:
- The field is a button that opens a dialog holding a real combobox: the search input with aria-activedescendant over a listbox (aria-multiselectable when picking several). Arrows move, Page Up/Down jump, Enter picks, Escape closes and returns focus, Backspace in an empty search removes the last chip. Typing on the closed field opens it with that letter.
- Counts ("8 results"), picks and removals are announced in a status region once typing settles; group names are visible labels, not options.
- Leaving rows and chips are their own detached elements, faded in a layer React never renders into, so they cost no render. Glides are measured from layout offsets right before each change and added to any glide still running.

items.accessibility:
- Five-field Unix cron: minute, hour, day, month, weekday, with names (MON, JAN), lists, ranges, steps, @daily-style shortcuts, L for the last day of the month, and FRI#2 or 5L for the nth or last weekday. 0 and 7 are Sunday. When both day and weekday are set, either one matching runs it, as in Unix cron; the sentence says so.
- English it reads: every N minutes or hours, from 9am to 5pm, weekdays, weekends, named days and ranges of them, the 1st and 15th, the last day, the second Tuesday, the last Friday, months, and times like 9, 9:30, 5pm, noon and midnight. What it can't say in cron ("9:30 and 17:00") it doesn't guess at.
- parseCron, describeCron, nextRuns and parseSchedule come from cron-parse.ts, which has no React in it, so a server or a worker can check and describe schedules the same way.
- The input has the field's label and is described by the sentence under it; errors mark it aria-invalid. The meaning is announced once typing pauses, never on each keystroke. Each run has its full text for screen readers; the rolling digits are hidden from them.
- Runs are worked out in the zone with Intl, day by day for up to six years, so a schedule that never fires (31 February) says so instead of hanging.
- Reduced motion: no glides, rolls or morphs; text and numbers change in place.

items.description: One panel, many features: the line slides between tabs, fills as autoplay runs, and the panel eases to each.

items.accessibility:
- A tree of treeitems with their level, position and open state. One row is in the tab order: ↑ ↓ move, → opens a row or steps into it, ← closes it or steps out to its parent, Home and End jump, typing a title's first letters jumps to it, Enter or Space chooses.
- Alt with ↑ or ↓ moves a row among its siblings, Alt+→ moves it into the row above, Alt+← moves it out after its parent. F2 renames and Delete deletes. Every move is announced with where it went.
- Carrying writes transforms only, to the copy, the line and the ring; rows are measured once when the carry starts (and again only when a row opens under it), and nothing re-renders until the drop. Rows are memoised, so opening a folder re-renders only the rows it changes.
- On touch the list scrolls as usual; holding a row for 300ms picks it up, and only then does the page stop scrolling. A chosen row shows its + and delete buttons, since there's no hover. Near the top or bottom of the tree (or the window) it scrolls.
- Reduced motion opens, closes and moves rows in place; the line, the ring, the amber refusal and the announcements still say what happens.
items.previewNote: Interactive local fixture. Data and async results are simulated in the preview; the caller supplies application services.

states.title: open
states.description: Opening a row turns its chevron (260ms) while its children fade in through a 4px blur where they land and the rows below glide down (480ms). Closing folds the children away where they stood while the rows below glide up. An open row with nothing inside says so.

states.title: lift
states.description: After 4px (or a 300ms hold on touch, with a short vibration where supported) a copy of the row lifts: a thin line ring and a "+3" count of what's inside it. The row and everything under it dim to 40% in place.

states.title: slot
states.description: The gap under the pointer gets a 2px line in the ring colour with a hollow dot at its start; the start is the depth the row will land at (90ms per change). Sideways movement changes the depth one indent at a time, inside the depths that gap allows.

states.title: into
states.description: Over the middle half of a row that holds others, a ring and a light wash surround it: the row will go inside, at the end. Held there 650ms, a closed row with rows inside opens; rows opened this way close again if nothing was dropped in them.

states.title: refuse
states.description: When canDrop returns a reason, the line or ring turns amber and the reason appears under the carried copy. Let go and the copy springs home (300ms, slight overshoot); the reason stays a moment under the tree.

states.title: land
states.description: The moved row glides from where the copy was let go into its slot (480ms), its parent opening if it was closed; rows that changed depth slide sideways into their new indent. If onMove throws, everything glides back, the row shakes, and the line under the tree says so.

states.title: edit
states.description: F2 or a double-click turns the title into a field in place. + on a row grows a new row inside it with a field; Enter keeps it, Escape folds it away. Delete folds the row and everything inside it away and holds "Deleted … · Undo" over a draining thin line (paused on hover) before calling onDelete.

items.accessibility:
- The viewer is a top-layer popover with role="dialog" and aria-modal: it opens above everything without making the page inert, which on a large page restyles every element in the frame it opens. Focus is trapped inside, the page behind does not scroll, Escape closes and focus returns to the current thumbnail, including after browsing.
- Left and Right browse, Home and End jump to the first and last image. Buttons expose disabled states at the ends.
- Pointer cancellation restores the image. Horizontal swipes leave vertical touch movement to the browser.
- Reduced motion removes expansion, sliding, overshoot and thumbnail zoom. Navigation and all controls remain available.
- Image IDs must be unique; width and height should match the source asset. The component handles an empty collection.
- The entry point, viewer and motion helpers install together. No global animation stylesheet or animation library is required.

items.accessibility:
- Nodes are real buttons. Tab reaches every node and control; arrows move focus in supplied reading order. Alt + arrows move a node by 12 canvas pixels. Enter or Space opens details; Escape closes details or cancels a drag.
- Status uses text and icons as well as colour. Running, completion and error updates are announced in a polite live region.
- Reduced motion removes connection pulses, spinning indicators and eased viewport/panel transitions. Direct manipulation stays attached to the pointer.
- The canvas owns touch gestures inside its bounds. The initial zoom stays at least 85% for legibility; on narrow screens, pan to reach other nodes or use Fit for an overview. Focusing a node brings it into view.
- Node positions are remembered locally after dragging. onNodeMove lets you persist them. Remount with a new key to reset a moved layout.
- This is a workflow viewer, not a graph execution engine or connection editor. Your application owns execution, retries and data validation.

items.accessibility:
- The ruler is a slider: arrow keys step between releases, Home and End jump to the first and the latest, and its value reads as the version, title and date.
- Play is a real button whose label changes between "Play the releases" and "Pause"; dragging, swiping, the arrows or a key pause it.
- On touch the ruler takes the whole gesture, like any slider. The card takes only sideways swipes; vertical ones still scroll the page.
- The arrows are buttons labelled "Older release" and "Newer release"; at either end they are aria-disabled rather than disabled, so focus stays on them.
- The lens is CSS: each tick reads the playhead’s position from one custom property and works out its own height, so a frame of scrubbing is one style write and no layout. Frames run only while the playhead moves.
- Installs Number roll and Text morph. Uses container query units (cqw), in every current browser. With reduced motion the playhead jumps instead of gliding and play steps from release to release.

items.accessibility:
- The icon buttons are the accessible actions: they are real buttons in the tab order, shown on hover or focus, with the action as their name. The swipe cells repeat them for pointers and are hidden from assistive technology.
- Results are announced in a status region: done, or failed with an invitation to try again. Escape closes an open row.
- Only one row is open at a time, as in mail apps. A tap on an open row closes it instead of following whatever is under it, and a click that ends a drag is swallowed.
- Drags and trackpad swipes write transforms only, and one frame loop runs the spring and the arming, then sleeps. Each cell is a full-height layer moved by transform, so revealing never changes layout.
- Reduced motion turns springs, folds and the shake into immediate changes; the colours, labels and announcements still say what happened.

items.accessibility:
- A real tree for assistive tech: treeitems with level, position and expanded state, one tab stop. ↑ and ↓ move, → opens or steps in, ← closes or steps out, Home and End jump, Enter or Space toggles, / jumps to search, and ⌘C or Ctrl+C copies the value of the row you're on.
- Each row has a spoken label (key, value, and in a diff "added", "removed" or "was …"); match counts and copies are announced in a status region.
- Containers with more than 100 children show them a hundred at a time with "Show 100 more · 1,240 left"; a search reaches past that to show a match.
- json-tree.ts has no React in it: buildTree, diffTree, formatPath, searchTree and parseError work on a server too, e.g. to store the diff of an audit event.
- Strings, numbers and booleans use the same light and dark palette as Code block; diff marks use emerald, red and amber with a sign beside each, so colour is never the only signal.
- Reduced motion: folds, the chevron and the path change in place.

items.accessibility:
- Each column is a labelled section with an ordered list; each card says its name, column, place and amount. Space or Enter picks a card up, arrows carry it (up and down in its column, left and right across columns, skipping none: a column that refuses says why), Space drops it and Escape puts it back. Every step is announced, and onMove runs once, on the drop.
- While a card is carried the board writes transforms only: the card's own (with its tilt) and the shift of the cards making way. React re-renders only when the column or slot under it changes, for the chip and the totals. On the drop every card is snapshotted where it is on screen, the new order is laid out, and each glides from its snapshot.
- On touch, the board scrolls as usual; a 300ms hold picks a card up and only then does the page stop scrolling under the finger. Near the board's sides it scrolls sideways, near the window's edges the page scrolls. Narrow, columns snap one at a time.
- Reduced motion moves cards in place, without tilt, glides or shakes; chips, totals, amber refusals and the announcements still say what happened.

items.accessibility:
- The secret only ever lives in the component's state while it is on screen; it leaves the page once Done has folded it away. Store a hash on your server, never the key.
- The new key's Copy button takes focus as the secret opens; Done hands focus back to "Create key". Creating, rolling, revoking and hiding the secret are announced in a status region outside the list.
- Roll and Revoke ask first: the icon becomes a cross and the confirm button opens beside it. Escape, the cross, or a click or focus elsewhere takes the question back.
- The expiry countdown is hidden from screen readers (it would re-announce every second); they hear the time the key expires instead.
- Rows glide with additive transforms measured from layout offsets, and a revoked row folds away as its own detached element, so nothing re-renders for it.
- Reduced motion opens, seals and removes in place; the chip and the secret simply swap.

states.title: create

states.title: reveal

states.title: seal
states.description: Done closes the fold in 460ms. The secret's prefix and last four characters fly into the chip together, as words (540ms), the dots rise in between them and the chip's thin line fades in behind; everything else blurs out. The secret then leaves the page.

states.title: roll
states.description: The roll icon stretches into "Roll key". Once onRoll resolves, the chip lifts away through a blur and the new secret opens in the same row. If onRoll returns the old key with expiresAt, it fades in underneath as "Expires in 23:59:41", its numbers rolling down a second at a time.

states.title: revoke
states.description: The bin's circle stretches into a red "Revoke"; it spins, a check draws and the row dims for 700ms, then folds away while the rows below glide up. A failure shakes the button and says Try again.

states.title: last used

items.accessibility:
- Toggles are role="switch" buttons labelled by their field label and described by its description. Choices are radio groups: arrows move and select, and only the selected option is in the tab order.
- Every message under a field is linked to its input with aria-describedby, and inputs with errors are aria-invalid. Saves, refusals and resets are announced in a status region; the "Saving" beside a label is for the eye only.
- ⌘S or Ctrl+S saves while focus is in the form. The bar is a sticky footer: on a long page it stays at the bottom of the window while the form is in view.
- A newer change to a switch wins: an older answer that arrives late is ignored. Edits made while a save is running stay unsaved and keep the bar open.
- Text inputs use 16px type on touch screens so phones don't zoom into them.
- Reduced motion changes everything in place: no thrown thumbs, slides, swells or shakes; the words and colours still say what happened.

states.title: check
states.description: 450ms after typing stops, check() runs: a spinner sits at the end of the field and "Checking" lifts in under it, then a drawn check and "Available", or the reason in red with a red thin line. A newer keystroke cancels the older check through its AbortSignal.

states.title: server errors
states.description: Throw SettingsFormError(message, { field: reason }) and each reason opens under its field, the field shakes, the bar shows the message and focus moves to the first field with an error.

states.title: reset

items.accessibility:

- Errors are linked to their field with aria-describedby and the field is marked aria-invalid. The resend countdown is hidden from screen readers; the button says when it can be used.
- The card never stores the password or code and never calls a service itself.
- Inputs use 16px type on touch screens so phones don't zoom into them.
- Reduced motion changes steps in place: no shrinking frame, slides, shakes or drawing; the words still say what happened.

items.accessibility:
- Each endpoint is a button with aria-expanded; its details are its own region. Deliveries are a list whose rows open with aria-expanded, and Request / Response is a tablist that arrows move between.
- The test result ("200 OK in 182 ms") is a status message; adding, deleting, toggling and redelivering are announced too. The wire itself is for the eye only.
- Status codes are told by number and word, not colour alone: 2xx emerald, 3xx and 4xx amber, 5xx and no answer red.
- The bead and the pulse are Web Animations that only run while a test is in flight; deliveries glide with additive transforms (use-row-motion).
- Reduced motion skips the bead, the pulse, the fades and the glides; results and rows still change in place.

features.title: Paste a URL, get a domain
features.description: A pasted address is cut down to its host. Anything that is not a domain shakes the field and says so.

features.title: Records you can copy
features.description: Each record opens with its own copy buttons, named after the record, such as “Copy CNAME value”.

features.title: It checks again by itself
features.description: Checks wait longer each time and never run while the tab is hidden. “Checking again in 0:42” counts down, and Check now asks at once.

features.title: Records tick green
features.description: Each record turns green the moment your server sees it, and the rail above fills record by record.

features.title: From certificate to Live
features.description: It shows “Issuing certificate”, then Live. The records fold behind “Show records” and the address becomes a link.

features.title: Failures in plain words

states.title: add
states.description: A pasted URL becomes its host on paste ("https://App.Fernhill.co/pricing" → "app.fernhill.co"). Anything that isn't a domain shakes the field and says so. Connect turns to Connecting while onAdd runs.

states.title: added
states.description: The field folds away in 480ms while the domain opens; its heading travels 620ms from where the address sat in the field. The records rise in one after another, 70ms apart.

states.title: waiting
states.description: A pinging amber dot says "Waiting for DNS", then "1 of 2 records found". "Checking again in 0:42" rolls down a second at a time; while check() runs it reads "Checking DNS" with a spinner.

states.title: found
states.description: A record that verifies swaps its spinner for a drawn check, says Found and glows green for 1.4s; the rail fills to that record's share of the first step in 760ms.

states.title: certificate
states.description: With every record found the status morphs to "Issuing certificate" and the middle step spins until your server reports the domain active.

states.title: live
states.description: The rail runs to its end, each step draws its check, "Live" turns green, the records fold behind "Show records" and the heading becomes a link to the domain.

states.title: failed
states.description: Your server's message opens under the records in red and automatic checks stop; the wrong record is marked. Check now starts again.

props.name: onAdd
props.description: – · Registers the domain (already cut down to its host) and returns { domain, status, records, message? }. Throw to keep the field and show the message.

props.name: check
props.description: – · Reports what your server sees now. Called on the schedule and by Check now; the signal aborts it when the domain is removed or a newer check starts.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: – · Removes the domain; the card goes back to the field. Without it there is no Remove.

props.name: value
props.description: – · Controlled state. status is "pending", "issuing", "active" or "failed"; each record is { type, name, value, priority?, status? }.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: – · A domain that was already added, when uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: – · Every add, check and removal.

props.name: schedule
props.description: [10, 20, 30, 60, 120, 300] · Seconds before each automatic check; the last one repeats. Checks wait while the tab is hidden.

props.name: title
props.description: "Custom domain" · The card's heading.

props.name: description
props.description: – · The line under the heading.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: "app.yourcompany.com" · The field's placeholder and the example in its error.

items.accessibility:
- The scrolling area is focusable and scrolls with the keyboard. Lines are a list; lines with data are buttons with aria-expanded. The list is not a live region, so a busy tail never floods a screen reader; pausing and resuming are announced instead.
- "/" focuses search while focus is inside the stream; Escape clears it.
- Rows use content-visibility, so a thousand lines lay out only what's on screen, and each row is memoised on its own line: a new batch renders only the new rows.
- Levels are told by word as well as colour: "err" and "warn" in red and amber, with a 2px tick at the line's edge.
- Reduced motion drops the fades, the pill's rise, the ping and the smooth scroll; lines still arrive and the counts still change.

features.title: Pinned until you scroll up
features.description: New lines are drawn once per frame however fast they arrive, and only your own scroll lets go of the bottom.

features.title: It counts what you missed
features.description: A “↓ 128 new” pill rises with its count rolling, and one tap takes you back down.

features.title: Pause without losing lines
features.description: Live becomes Paused and holds lines back (“Paused · 42 waiting”). Live plays them in again.

features.title: Levels and search
features.description: Level chips count lines as they arrive, search marks every match, and / focuses it.

features.title: Lines open into their fields
features.description: A line with data opens under itself into its fields, with a Copy button.

features.title: Older lines on demand
features.description: Reaching the top loads earlier lines above without moving the line you are reading.

states.title: tail
states.description: Pushed lines are collected and rendered once per animation frame. Up to 12 new lines fade in from a 2px blur (260ms); bigger bursts simply appear. Each commit ends on the newest line while the view is pinned.

states.title: reading
states.description: A scroll you make (wheel, touch, keys or the scrollbar) lets go; content changing size never does. New lines keep arriving and the pill rises 10px into place (420ms) with its count rolling. Tapping it scrolls down smoothly and pins the view again; so does scrolling back to the bottom.

states.title: paused
states.description: The green pinging dot turns grey and Live morphs to Paused; lines are held, and "· 42 waiting" opens beside it, rolling. Live plays them in as one batch.

states.title: filter
states.description: Level chips count every line in memory (the numbers roll) and hide their level when switched off. Search marks every match in the message and keeps only lines that match the message or source.

states.title: open
states.description: A line with data is a button; it opens by height in 320ms into a thin line box of its fields (numbers in the primary colour, strings quoted) with a Copy that morphs to Copied.

states.title: earlier
states.description: With loadEarlier, reaching the top loads older lines above; the scroll position is corrected in the same frame, so the line you were reading doesn't move. An empty answer says "Start of the log".

props.name: subscribe
props.description: – · Starts the tail. Call push with one line or many, as often as you like; return a function that stops it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: – · Lines to start with, oldest first: { id, at, level, message, source?, data? }.

props.name: loadEarlier
props.description: – · Loads lines older than the first one, oldest first. Return an empty list when there are no more.

props.name: max
props.description: 1000 · Lines kept while the view is pinned to the bottom. While you're reading further up nothing is dropped.

props.name: height
props.description: 420 · The scrolling area's height.

props.name: title
props.description: "Logs" · Names the list and the search field for screen readers.

items.name: cavemio-log-stream
items.title: Log stream
items.description: A live tail you can actually read: scroll up and it lets go while a "↓ 128 new" pill counts what arrives, with pause, level counts, search and lines that open into their fields.

items.accessibility:
- The drop target is the label of a real file input: Tab reaches it, Enter or Space opens the picker, and its focus ring shows on the target.
- Matching works without a pointer: every field's pill opens a listbox (arrows, typing a name, Enter), and clicking a column then a field matches them too. Threads are drawn for the eye; screen readers hear the pills.
- Problem cells are real inputs marked aria-invalid with their reason under them. The import bar is a progressbar with the row counts as its values. Each step's result is announced in a status region.
- Nothing leaves the browser until onImport: parsing, matching and checking all happen on the page.
- Reduced motion swaps steps in place and draws threads and checks at once.

features.title: Big files don’t freeze the page
features.description: The file is read in slices with a pause between them. 200,000 rows take about a quarter of a second.

features.title: Columns match themselves
features.description: Columns that match a field by name, ignoring case and punctuation, are already threaded. Carry a column onto a field, or use its dropdown, to change it.

features.title: Checked before anything is sent
features.description: Every row is checked first, and the counts read like “2,996 ready · 4 need a look”.

features.title: Fix problems in place
features.description: Rows with problems open with their bad cells as fields. Fix one and it folds away, or skip what is left.

features.title: Sent in batches
features.description: Rows go to your onImport function in batches with a progress bar. Cancel stops after the batch in flight.

states.title: drop
states.description: Dragging a file over the target turns its edge blue and lifts the icon 4px with a slight overshoot; the line morphs to "Drop to read it". A file that isn't CSV, is empty or is over maxRows shakes the target and says why.

states.title: read
states.description: The file is parsed in 200,000-character slices with a pause between (200,000 rows take about a quarter of a second), the icon spinning. The separator is taken from the first line.

states.title: match
states.description: Steps slide in 28px from the right while the card eases to its height. Columns that match a field by name, ignoring case and punctuation ("E-mail address" → Email), are threaded on arrival; each thread draws itself in 520ms. Carrying a column trails a dashed thread and lights the field under the pointer. Each field's pill grows into the list of columns, a sample under every name; narrow cards show only the fields and their pills.

states.title: review
states.description: Every row is checked (required fields, then validate). The ready and need-a-look counts roll. Rows with problems show their bad cells as inputs with a red thin line and the reason; when a row is right its badge morphs to Fixed, and 650ms later it folds away.

states.title: import
states.description: Ready rows go to onImport in batches of batchSize. The bar fills by transform; the count rolls. Cancel aborts the signal and stops after the batch in flight. A batch that throws marks its rows as skipped with the error's message.

states.title: done
states.description: A ring draws in 640ms, then a check. If anything was skipped or refused, "Skipped rows" downloads them as CSV with a column saying why.

props.name: fields
props.description: – · { key, label, required?, match?, validate? }. match lists other column names to recognise; validate returns why a value won't do.

props.name: onImport
props.description: – · Saves one batch of rows shaped { [key]: value }. Return failed: [{ index, reason }] for rows your server refused; throw to mark the whole batch skipped.

props.name: batchSize
props.description: 250 · Rows per onImport call.

props.name: maxRows
props.description: 50000 · Files with more rows are refused before matching.

props.name: noun
props.description: { one: "row", many: "rows" } · What a row is, for the counts and buttons.

props.name: templateHref
props.description: – · A "Download a template" link under the drop target.

props.name: title
props.description: "Import" · The card's heading.

props.name: description
props.description: – · The line under the heading.

props.name: onDone
props.description: – · After the last batch, e.g. to refresh the list behind it.

props.name: ref
props.description: – · load(text, name?) reads text as if it were a dropped file, e.g. from a paste or a sample.

items.accessibility:

states.title: connect
states.description: Connect turns to Connecting with a spinner the moment it's clicked; onConnect is called in the same click, so a window it opens isn't blocked.

states.title: connected

states.title: refused

states.title: filter

states.title: disconnect

props.type: (url, { name?, width?, height?, type?, timeout? }) => Promise<data>

items.accessibility:
- The overall line is a heading; each service names its bars, says its status in words and describes how to read them. The day card is drawn for the eye; keyboard reading announces each day in a status region instead.
- Colour is never the only signal: every service says Operational, Degraded, Outage or Maintenance, and every day says what happened in words.
- One card serves all the bars of a service, so ninety bars carry no tooltips or listeners of their own.
- The overall dot pings only while something is wrong.
- Reduced motion draws the bars at once, moves the card without gliding and swaps sentences in place.

states.title: overall
states.description: Derived from the services: any outage reads "Major outage" (red), any degradation "Some systems degraded" (amber), maintenance "Maintenance in progress", otherwise "All systems operational" (emerald). The sentence lifts out and in through a blur; a dot pings while something is wrong.

states.title: days
states.description: On mount every bar scales up from the baseline (520ms, 5ms apart, left to right). Operational days are emerald, degraded amber, outages red, maintenance grey and days without data a thin line outline. Containers under 32rem show the last 30 days.

states.title: read
states.description: Hovering a bar dims the others to 55% and one card glides to sit over it (320ms), clamped inside the row: the date, what happened ("Degraded for 1 h 2 min") and the incidents that touched it.

states.title: keys
states.description: Each service's bars are one tab stop. Focus starts on today; arrows move a day, Home and End jump to the ends, Escape hides the card. Each day is read out as you move.

states.title: incident
states.description: Open incidents sit above the services with a coloured edge by impact. A new update fades down 6px out of a blur on top of the list; the stage pill morphs and turns green when resolved. Resolved incidents fold into "Past incidents", whose count rolls.

states.title: changes
states.description: When a service's status changes its word morphs and its colour eases over 500ms; today's bar recolours in place.

props.name: services
props.description: – · { id, name, status ("operational" | "degraded" | "major" | "maintenance"), uptime?, days }. days are oldest first, the last one today: { date: "2026-10-14", status, minutes?, incidents? }.

props.name: incidents
props.description: – · { id, title, impact ("minor" | "major" | "maintenance"), stage, services?, updates }. updates are newest first: { id, at, stage, message }. Resolved ones fold into Past incidents.

props.name: updatedAt
props.description: – · When the data was checked; shown as "Updated 2 min ago" and kept current.

props.name: title
props.description: "Status" · Read before the overall line by screen readers.

items.name: cavemio-status-bars
items.title: Status bars
items.description: A status page that reads at a glance: ninety days a service drawn up bar by bar, one card that glides between them, and incidents whose updates open in as they're posted.

items.accessibility:
- People take the five chart colours in the order they first appear and keep them; pass color to choose your own.
- The cursors are decoration to assistive tech; what people say is announced through a polite status region, once per message.
- Positions are fractions, so the same numbers work on a phone and a wide screen as long as what’s underneath scales the same way.
- "/" is only taken while your pointer is over the area, so a page’s own "/" shortcut (search, usually) keeps working everywhere else.
- The loop sleeps when nobody is moving. With reduced motion cursors jump to where they are and bubbles change size in place.

states.title: move
states.description: A spring (stiffness 150, damping 24) per cursor, run in one requestAnimationFrame loop that writes transforms directly and stops once everyone has settled. Someone new appears where they are.

states.title: say

states.title: click

states.title: idle / leave

states.title: you

props.name: cursors
props.type: { id, name, x, y, color?, message?, clicks?, selection? }[]

props.name: children

props.name: idleAfter

props.name: onCursorMove

props.name: onMessage

items.accessibility:
- The map is decorative to assistive tech; each new event’s label and detail are announced through a polite status region.
- Points use plain latitude and longitude; the projection is a stretched equirectangular, so it reads like the maps people know without a library.
- The coastlines are deliberately coarse; at this dot size the detail wouldn’t show. Antarctica and the far north are cropped.
- Installs Text morph. With reduced motion nothing ripples, glides or draws; pings simply light their dots.

items.accessibility:
- Grey in a new shadcn project? Its default theme sets --chart-1 to --chart-5 to greys. Set five colours, light and dark, as in Theming › Chart colours (/ui/theming#charts).
- The shape switch is a radio group (arrow keys move and choose). Dragging the thumb is a pointer extra on top of it; it only starts from the selected shape, and a short press is still a click.
- The plot is one tab stop: arrow keys, Home and End read each point, Escape lets go, and the reading is announced. Every value is also in a visually hidden table.
- One frame loop writes path data and two transforms straight to the DOM and sleeps when nothing moves; nothing re-renders through React during a morph, a scrub or a slide of the bead.
- The line is a monotone cubic, so it never overshoots a value between two points, and the bead and the area's edge are evaluated on the same curve.
- Colour comes from the theme's --chart-1 (falling back to --primary). Reduced motion changes shape, data and the bead in place, and turns the thumb's drag off.

states.title: arrive
states.description: The first time the card is on screen every mark rises from the axis (650ms, up to 40ms apart) and the total and the scale roll up from zero.

states.title: bars → line
states.description: Each bar bulges a touch, pinches to a stick and retracts up into a 7px bead on its value, which hops 2px as it closes (460ms, staggered left to right). A thread then draws from the left through the beads (an exact cut of the curve, not a dash), and each bead shrinks to the thread's thickness under it as the tip passes. About 1.2s.

states.title: line → bars
states.description: The thread's tail is pulled to the right. Each bead swells back just before the tail leaves it, then lifts, drips a stick to the axis and spreads a little past the bar's width as it lands before settling (540ms).

states.title: line ↔ area
states.description: The fill pours down from the line to the axis, left to right (760ms), and drains back up into it on the way back (620ms). The wash fades from 22% at the top to 3% at the axis.

states.title: bars ↔ area
states.description: The bars widen until they touch and the solid fill fades to the wash; the steps they make melt into the curve while the line draws along the top. The reverse sets the curve into steps and parts them into bars.

states.title: scrub
states.description: Drag the thumb of the switch: the morph between neighbouring shapes is held at the frame under your finger. Let go and it runs on to the nearer shape, or the one you flung it toward; the thumb lands with a slight overshoot.

states.title: take it back
states.description: Choose the shape you came from while a morph is running and it runs backward from that frame. A third shape waits for the morph to land, then goes on.

states.title: data
states.description: New values ease to their heights one after another (650ms) while the scale's labels roll; on the line and the area the curve reshapes as they go.

states.title: hover
states.description: Bars dim to 32% except the one you're on. On the line and the area a ringed bead slides along the curve to the point (it rides the line, never cutting across it) with a thin line under it. The figure rolls to the point and its name morphs into the caption.

- The plot is one focusable group: ←/→ move between buckets, Home and End jump to the ends, Escape lets go. Each step is announced in a polite region (date, value, the period before, the note); the pointer path isn't announced.
- Every value is also in a visually hidden table with the period before as a column.
- The line is a monotone cubic, so it never overshoots a point: a day with zero visitors never dips below the axis.
- Its height steps down in narrow containers (a container query), the tick labels thin out to fit, and labels near an edge hang inward instead of running off the card. On touch, pressing reads a bucket; the brush keeps vertical page scroll.
- Reduced motion: no reveal, morph, stretch or glide; the line, the readout and the scale change in place.

items.accessibility: Native labeled buttons and sliders, focus-preserving keyboard menus, scoped shortcuts, touch controls, cinematic focus containment and restoration, live reduced motion. On the focused frame: Space/K play, arrows seek/volume, M mute, F fullscreen, C captions. Shortcuts do not consume input fields or button keys.
items.previewNote: Seven interactive examples cover formats, quality, diagnostics, engine comparison, motion and authorized DRM tests. Public media loads from its original host. DRM success is shown only after the protected stream plays. Browser fullscreen/PiP and commercial CDMs depend on device support. See the source registry documentation and docs/video-player.md for full integration and verification guidance.

useCases.title: HLS and DASH
useCases.description: Use Shaka for adaptive HLS/DASH and protected streams. Select HLS.js explicitly for HLS. Native playback has fewer quality and diagnostic capabilities.

useCases.title: Compose a player
useCases.description: Set controls={false} and render VideoControls, VideoPlayButton, VideoSeekbar, VideoVolume, or VideoSettings as children. useVideoState selects stable fields; useVideoPlayer exposes normalized actions.

useCases.title: Protected playback
useCases.description: Pass source.drm.servers keyed by com.widevine.alpha, com.microsoft.playready, or com.apple.fps. Advanced Shaka configuration supports certificates and license headers. Use HTTPS, authorized assets, and runtime credentials. FairPlay requires device-specific packaging and certificates; the demo does not certify it.

features.title: One persistent video
features.description: GSAP interpolates the existing frame geometry into the top layer. No media reload occurs during cinematic expansion. Browser fullscreen is a separate API.

features.title: Observable playback
features.description: Real bandwidth estimates, rendition bitrate, frame drops, buffer ranges and errors. N/A identifies unavailable measurements. Hidden diagnostics stop polling.

features.title: Source installation
features.description: React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4 and shadcn theme tokens are required. All helpers ship in this registry item; only the selected streaming engine loads at runtime in a splitting bundler.

states.title: Adaptive or fixed quality
states.description: Auto enables ABR. Manual requests retain buffered segments, so the active rendition may change later. Changing audio returns to Auto to avoid pinning an incompatible variant.

states.title: Buffering and recovery
states.description: Media/engine events drive loading feedback. Shaka requests retry up to three times with backoff; HLS.js allows two additional fatal recovery attempts. Retry starts a fresh session.

states.title: Browser limitations and troubleshooting
states.description: Check CORS on manifests, segments, captions and licenses, HTTPS, codecs, MSE/EME support, and autoplay policy. Diagnostics omit credentials. Iframe permission policy can block fullscreen/PiP/DRM; test natively.

props.name: src / source
props.description: URL or typed source including format, poster, and caller-provided Shaka DRM configuration. Explicit type is required for extensionless HLS/DASH URLs. Keep DRM configuration referentially stable.

props.name: type
props.description: Optional format hint; otherwise detected from the URL extension.

props.name: engine
props.description: Lazy-load one engine. HLS.js accepts HLS only and falls back to native HLS when MSE is unavailable. Engine changes reload media and restore time for the same URL.

props.name: poster / title
props.description: Poster URL and accessible video title. Source poster takes precedence.

props.name: autoPlay / muted / loop
props.description: Browser media preferences. Autoplay can be rejected by browser policy; user play remains available.

props.name: playing / onPlayingChange
props.description: Optional controlled playback intent and actual media-event callback. Omit playing for local control.

props.name: controls
props.description: Show the default control composition. Set false and compose exported controls or use onReady for a custom interface.

props.name: enableGooey
props.description: SVG filtering applies only to decorative surfaces. False uses a static, unfiltered fallback.

props.name: enableAnimations / reducedMotion
props.description: GSAP motion toggle and reduced-motion preview. OS reduced-motion settings always take precedence; changes settle active motion.

props.name: enableDiagnostics
props.description: Lazy-load genuine engine/browser metrics and a bounded event timeline. Polls at 1Hz only while the panel is visible; copy exports sanitized JSON.

props.name: enablePictureInPicture / enableFullscreen
props.description: Enable PiP and fullscreen controls. The main fullscreen button animates viewport expansion; Settings offers browser fullscreen where supported. Unavailable browser actions are disabled and failed requests are announced.

props.name: onReady
props.description: Receives normalized play, pause, seek, quality, audio, captions, volume, speed, and retry actions.

props.name: onError
props.description: Sanitized error code/category with fatal and retryable flags. Raw URLs, DRM payloads, and tokens are omitted.

props.name: className / style / children
props.description: Wrapper customization and composable overlay content. useVideoPlayer/useVideoState expose normalized controls and state.
